title: trqp serve: bind failures exit with a traceback; IPv6 --bind unsupported
description: git-vouch-trqp:366-369, 389-396. ThreadingHTTPServer((bind, port), ...) is not guarded. Reproduced: '--port 22' gives a PermissionError traceback, a port in use gives OSError EADDRINUSE through the same path, and '--bind ::1' gives 'socket.gaierror: Address family for hostname not supported', because HTTPServer.address_family is always AF_INET. --help says 'address' with no IPv4-only caveat. What goes wrong: common operator mistakes (port taken, unprivileged low port, an IPv6 proxy upstream) end in a raw traceback instead of a one-line error, unlike the sibling git-vouch's no-traceback rule (see vouch-88xy), and IPv6 binding is impossible. Fix: catch OSError around server construction, print 'git-vouch-trqp: cannot listen on {bind}:{port}: {e.strerror}' to stderr and return 1. For IPv6, either say 'IPv4 address' in --bind help (constraint) or pick the address family from socket.getaddrinfo(bind, port)[0][0] in a one-line subclass, as http.server's own CLI does. Test: start serve on an already-bound port, assert exit 1 and no 'Traceback' in stderr.
close_reason: bind failure exits 1 with one line; IPv6 literal binds AF_INET6, names and '' stay IPv4 (test_serve_on_a_port_in_use_fails_cleanly, test_serve_binds_ipv6, test_serve_binds_names_and_all_on_ipv4, test_serve_wants_a_port)
